items.name: Recovery test — failover into us-east-2 (dev)
preconditions: Phase 0 checklist green and signed off
Every Tier-0 store has a current replication path, checked today (Phase 0 item 2)
Operator and approver both on the calendar for the full window
T0 definition agreed: T0 = the first failover action is executed (the recovery-region apply)

steps.title: Pre-flight: record T0 and prove every replication path is current
steps.detail: Open the test record and write wall-clock T0 the moment the first failover action runs. Then read each mechanism's own freshness signal, because current lag IS your RPA if the event is now: Aurora Global Database replica lag (adjudication), the age of the newest AWS Backup copy (pricing), ReplicationStatus on recently written objects (S3 CRR), replication state on the newest image tags (ECR), replica presence for every secret on the signed-off list, and — for the two components still on point-in-time recovery, the remittance cluster and the claim queues — recovery points from the same aligned sync. Screenshot the lot: this is the RPA evidence.
steps.verify: Global-cluster lag under a minute; CRR ReplicationStatus COMPLETED on recent objects; ECR tags present in us-east-2; replica secrets present; the two point-in-time stores showing aligned recovery points none older than 30 min
steps.pass: Every in-scope store has a recorded, current position; screenshots in the record
steps.record: T0; per-store lag or recovery-point age

steps.title: Pre-flight: confirm the drill is contained (no path to a real partner)
steps.detail: Containment stays ON for tests — it is what stops a drill POSTing a real claim to the clearinghouse, uploading a real settlement file, or firing a real webhook. In this estate that means two things, because the estate is recovered two ways: the recovery-region VPC has no egress route to partner endpoints (the IaC-rebuilt side), and the third-party tool's network sandbox stays enabled for the resources it recovers. AWS itself is still reachable — image pulls and secrets go over VPC endpoints (ecr.api, ecr.dkr, the S3 GATEWAY endpoint, because ECR layers live in S3 and without it pulls fail after the manifest and look like a mystery network fault — plus secretsmanager, sts, kms, logs). Relaxing containment needs a named approver AND a containment probe run from inside the recovered environment showing zero reachable partner endpoints. See decision dec_sandbox_v2.
steps.verify: No route from the recovery VPC to any partner endpoint; the endpoint list is complete; the vendor sandbox is enabled for the resources it recovers
steps.pass: Containment proven — or, if relaxed, the approver name and a clean containment probe are both recorded

steps.title: Prove the image path before anything needs it
steps.detail: ECR replication runs continuously, so the images should already be in us-east-2 — "should" is the word this step exists to remove. Confirm all 17 repositories and the expected tags are present, then prove a real pull from inside the recovery VPC over the endpoints. Images pushed before the replication rule was created were never replicated, and repository settings and lifecycle policies do not replicate at all.
steps.command: aws ecr describe-repositories --region us-east-2 --query "length(repositories)" && aws ecr describe-images --repository-name adjudication --region us-east-2 --query "imageDetails[0].imageTags"
steps.verify: All 17 repositories present with the tags the deployments reference, and a test pull succeeds from the recovery VPC
steps.pass: Repositories and tags present; pull succeeds without internet egress
steps.record: Repository/tag count; any tag missing in the recovery region

steps.title: Build the recovery-region estate
steps.detail: Apply the recovery-region IaC — VPC, EKS and node pools, queues, API Gateway and VPC Link — and start the point-in-time recovery of the two components that are not continuously replicated (the remittance cluster and the claim queues). Do NOT promote the Aurora global cluster yet: that is the L3 data gate and it is the step with production consequences. Cold-start duration from here is the number leadership asks about — last measured ~40 min.
steps.verify: Apply completes with no failed resources; the point-in-time restores report done
steps.record: Apply start/finish; failed or skipped resources

steps.title: Verify platform: nodes, mesh, DNS, controllers
steps.detail: Nodes Ready, CoreDNS resolving, istiod up, ALB controller and Karpenter running. Do not look at app pods yet — a broken platform makes every app failure a red herring.
steps.command: kubectl get nodes && kubectl get pods -n kube-system && kubectl get pods -n istio-system
steps.verify: All nodes Ready; CoreDNS/istiod/ALB controller/Karpenter Running

steps.title: Verify data layer: fail over, promote, and measure freshness
steps.detail: Fail the Aurora global cluster over to us-east-2 and record the replica lag at the moment of failover — that IS the adjudication RPA, and it is the whole point of the global cluster. Then, from a pod in the recovery VPC, run the freshness query against the remittance cluster, which came back from a recovery point instead: age at T0 = its measured RPA (last test: 118 min against a 30 min configuration, because the points were not aligned). Confirm the queues exist; in-flight loss is accepted and documented, not discovered here.
steps.verify: Global cluster serving writes in us-east-2 with its lag recorded; the restored clusters answer; freshness recorded per DB
steps.pass: Data reachable; an RPA number written down for EVERY store, not just the fast one
steps.record: Measured RPA per database, with the mechanism next to it

steps.title: Verify secrets: the app’s own identity can decrypt them (tests die HERE)
steps.detail: `describe-secret` proves only that a secret exists — not its value, not that KMS will decrypt it, and not that the workload’s identity may read it. Prove the real thing: run `get-secret-value` (which forces kms:Decrypt) AS THE WORKLOAD’S OWN IDENTITY, with `sts get-caller-identity` beside it so the evidence shows the app role and not an admin. Best: exec into the real workload. Next best: a probe pod bound to the same ServiceAccount. Otherwise: the app’s own secrets-init probe passing.
steps.command: kubectl exec -n <tier0-ns> deploy/<workload> -- sh -c 'aws sts get-caller-identity; aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id <name> --query SecretString --output text >/dev/null && echo DECRYPT_OK'
steps.verify: Caller identity IS the application role, and every runtime secret returns DECRYPT_OK
steps.pass: DECRYPT_OK for every secret the workload mounts, proven under the app role — not an admin

steps.title: Verify applications: pods up, images from us-east-2 registry
steps.detail: Confirm adjudication, remittance, pharmacy and pricing are all Ready after the GitOps sync — and that every image reference points at the us-east-2 registry. A pod pulling cross-region from us-east-1 passes the test and fails the disaster.
steps.command: kubectl get deploy -A && kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | sort -u
steps.verify: Tier-0/1 deployments Ready; zero images referencing us-east-1

steps.title: Verify edge WITHOUT touching DNS
steps.detail: Hit the recovered API Gateway execute-api endpoint directly with a Host header for the real domain. Public DNS is never changed in Phase 1.
steps.verify: HTTP 200 through API GW → VPC Link → NLB → recovered pods

steps.title: Success bar 1: test claim answered end-to-end
steps.detail: Submit the partner-shaped test claim against the direct endpoint. A real adjudication response with a claim_id — not a 500 — is what 'recovered' means. First success = T1.
steps.pass: Claim adjudicated end-to-end; T1 recorded; RTA = T1 − T0

steps.title: Success bar 2: settlement path runs
steps.detail: Kick the remittance import against the recovered bucket/queue and confirm rows land in the recovered remittance Aurora. Front-door success with a dead settlement path is still an outage for finance.
steps.command: kubectl -n remittance create job --from=cronjob/era-import dr-test-import && kubectl logs -f job/dr-test-import
steps.verify: Import completes; rows in recovered remittance DB

steps.title: Conclude: no failback and no teardown without explicit approval
steps.detail: Teardown or failback only on the approver's written go. Both directions have production consequences here — failing the Aurora global cluster back to us-east-1 is a real switchover of a real cluster, and concluding the vendor recovery destroys the restored copies — and the standing decision forbids reflexive failback during tests.
steps.verify: Written approval from the named approver in the channel

steps.title: Triage findings same-day: gaps, tickets, runbook edits
steps.detail: Write the record while it hurts. Every surprise becomes a gap with severity, a ticket, or an edit to this runbook — usually all three.
steps.verify: Every finding has a gap id or ticket next to it
steps.pass: Record written same day; findings filed

rollback.title: Return the estate to its steady state
rollback.detail: After approval: destroy the recovery-region test stack, conclude the vendor recovery for the two point-in-time components, and then re-verify that every replication path is green again — global cluster replicating, CRR status COMPLETED on new objects, ECR rules healthy, replica secrets present, backup copies resuming. A test that leaves replication broken has negative value.
rollback.verify: Recovery-region test resources gone; every replication path reporting green
rollback.pass: Replicating again in every mechanism; no orphaned us-east-2 resources billing
rollback.record: Teardown time; time until every path was green again

items.notes: Phase 1 only — DNS and live traffic untouched. Most of this estate comes back from continuous AWS-native replication plus an IaC rebuild; two components (the remittance Aurora cluster and the claim queues) come back from third-party point-in-time recovery, which is why steps 1 and 6 ask for a recovery-point age as well as a replica lag. The August run died at step 7 (secrets); the signed-off list now exists and must be re-verified before the September run.
